## WhatsApp 24-Hour Messaging Window Explained

The WhatsApp 24-hour messaging window is the period in which a business can reply to a customer using free-form session messages after the customer sends a message. Once 24 hours have passed since the customer’s last message, the business generally needs to use an approved WhatsApp message template to start or continue the conversation.

This rule applies mainly to businesses using the WhatsApp Business Platform, including the Cloud API and solutions provided through an official WhatsApp Business Solution Provider. It is different from casually replying to customers through the WhatsApp Business app, where conversations are handled manually and the platform has fewer API-related controls.

Understanding the 24-hour window matters if your organisation uses WhatsApp for customer support, admissions, clinic enquiries, order updates, donations, bookings, or lead follow-up. A team that does not track the window can accidentally send non-compliant messages, delay customer replies, or assume that a message has been delivered when WhatsApp has restricted it.

## What Is the WhatsApp 24-Hour Messaging Window?

The 24-hour messaging window starts when a customer sends a message to your business number. It does not normally start when your business sends an outbound message.

For example, if a customer messages your clinic at 10:00 am on Monday, your team can generally send free-form replies until 10:00 am on Tuesday. If the customer sends another message at 4:00 pm on Monday, the window is usually extended from that new customer message and remains open until 4:00 pm on Tuesday.

The important event is the customer’s latest message. A business reply does not reset the 24-hour period.

Within this window, your team can usually send session messages such as:

- Text replies
- Images and documents
- Location details
- Audio or video, where supported by your setup
- Interactive buttons and lists
- Order or appointment information
- Clarifying questions
- Links relevant to the active conversation

These messages must still follow WhatsApp’s Business Messaging Policy, Commerce Policy, and other applicable rules. The open window does not give permission to send unrelated promotions, prohibited content, or messages that the customer did not reasonably expect.

### A simple example

A customer sends:

> “I want to know whether your school has admissions open for Class 5.”

Your admissions coordinator replies:

> “Admissions are open. Please share the child’s date of birth and your preferred campus.”

The customer responds with the details. The team can continue asking relevant questions, send a prospectus, share the admissions form, and explain the next steps through session messages while the window is open.

If the customer stops replying and the 24-hour period ends, the team should not send another ordinary free-form follow-up such as:

> “Just checking if you are still interested.”

Instead, the business may need to send an approved template, provided the customer has given the required consent and the message fits an allowed template category.

## Why WhatsApp Uses a 24-Hour Window

The rule is designed to distinguish customer-initiated service conversations from unsolicited business messaging.

When a customer contacts your organisation, WhatsApp treats the interaction as an active conversation. The business can respond naturally without selecting an approved template for every sentence. This is useful for support teams because real conversations do not always follow a fixed script.

After 24 hours without a customer message, WhatsApp treats a new business-initiated message differently. A business could otherwise send repeated sales, reminder, or promotional messages to people who contacted it once in the past. The window creates a boundary around that customer interaction.

The rule also supports a better customer experience:

- Customers receive help when they actively ask for it.
- Businesses can reply conversationally during the active session.
- Follow-ups outside the session require more structured approval.
- The business has to think about consent and message relevance.
- Automated systems are less likely to continue messaging indefinitely.

For Indian organisations, this distinction is particularly important when WhatsApp is connected to a CRM, website form, payment system, helpdesk, or chatbot. A system that sends messages automatically must know whether the conversation is open or whether a template is required.

## How the 24-Hour Window Works

### The customer’s message starts the window

The window normally begins when WhatsApp records a customer message to your business number. This could be a text message, image, document, voice note, button response, or another supported interaction.

Depending on the integration, a customer’s response to an interactive message may also be treated as a customer interaction. Your developer or WhatsApp provider should confirm how your particular setup records these events.

The business should not assume that sending a message from its side starts or extends the window.

### The latest customer message can extend it

Consider this timeline:

| Event | Time | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| Customer asks a question | Monday, 9:00 am | 24-hour window opens |
| Business replies | Monday, 9:10 am | Session continues; the timer does not reset |
| Customer sends more details | Monday, 3:00 pm | A new customer interaction is recorded |
| Business sends a document | Monday, 3:05 pm | Session message is allowed if relevant |
| No further customer reply | — | Window ends Tuesday, 3:00 pm |

The window is measured from the most recent qualifying customer message, not from the first message in the thread and not from your latest reply.

### The window is not a promise of delivery

A message can be allowed under the 24-hour rule and still fail to reach the customer. Delivery depends on factors such as:

- Whether the customer’s phone has internet access
- Whether the number is active
- Whether the customer has blocked the business
- Whether the message is rejected by policy or technical validation
- Whether the WhatsApp account or phone number has restrictions
- Whether media files meet size and format requirements
- Whether the integration is functioning correctly

The 24-hour rule answers one question: whether a business may send a particular type of message. It does not guarantee delivery, reading, or a response.

### Business hours do not pause the timer

If a customer messages at 6:00 pm on Friday, the 24-hour window does not normally wait until Monday morning. It continues through weekends and holidays.

This matters for schools, clinics, NGOs, and small teams that do not provide round-the-clock support. If you cannot reply during the open window, you may need to use an approved template later, or clearly communicate your working hours and expected response process.

## Session Messages Versus Template Messages

The simplest way to understand WhatsApp’s policy is to separate messages into two broad types.

### Session messages

Session messages are free-form replies sent during the open 24-hour customer service window. They are used to continue a conversation that the customer has recently started or re-opened.

Examples include:

- “Please share your order number so we can check this.”
- “The doctor is available at 4:30 pm or 6:00 pm. Which slot works for you?”
- “Here is the scholarship application form you requested.”
- “We have received your payment screenshot. Our accounts team is reviewing it.”
- “The nearest vaccination camp is at Kothrud Community Hall.”

The message should be connected to the customer’s request. An open session is not a licence to change the conversation into unrelated marketing.

### Template messages

A template message is a pre-approved message format used when the business initiates a message or when the 24-hour window has closed. Templates can contain variables, buttons, media headers, and other approved components, depending on the category and current WhatsApp requirements.

Common template categories include:

- Marketing
- Utility
- Authentication

A template must be submitted through the relevant WhatsApp Business Platform interface and approved before use. Approval does not mean every use is automatically acceptable. The message must still match the approved purpose, contain accurate information, and be sent to contacts who have given appropriate consent where required.

### Comparison table

| Point | Session message | Template message |
|---|---|---|
| When used | During an open 24-hour customer service window | When the window is closed or for business-initiated messaging |
| Format | Free-form conversation | Pre-approved structure |
| Typical use | Support, questions, troubleshooting, active enquiries | Reminders, updates, confirmations, re-engagement, authentication |
| Approval before sending | Usually not required for each message | Required for the template |
| Can it be promotional? | Should remain relevant to the active conversation | Marketing templates may be used if policy and consent requirements are met |
| Does a business reply reset the window? | No | No |
| Main risk | Sending irrelevant or prohibited content | Using the wrong category or sending without valid consent |

The terminology and pricing treatment can change as Meta updates WhatsApp Business Platform rules. Your provider should check the current policy and commercial terms before implementing a large messaging workflow.

## What Can You Send Inside the Window?

During an open customer conversation, a business can generally provide a normal support experience. The exact features depend on whether you use the WhatsApp Business app, Cloud API, or a provider’s dashboard.

### Customer support

Support teams can answer questions, troubleshoot issues, request information, and explain processes.

For a small business, this might include checking product availability or helping with a return. For an NGO, it might include explaining how to complete a donation or volunteer registration. For a school, it might include sending a fee structure requested by a parent.

Keep replies connected to the enquiry. If a parent asks about admissions, sending a separate campaign for unrelated summer activities may be treated differently from answering the admissions question.

### Documents and media

You can often send a document, image, or location during the active session. Examples include:

- An invoice requested by a customer
- A school prospectus
- A clinic preparation instruction sheet
- A map location
- A product image
- A receipt or acknowledgement
- A form or policy document

Before sending, check whether the document contains sensitive personal information. Avoid sharing one customer’s details in a group or sending a document to the wrong number.

### Interactive messages

Buttons and list menus can make customer conversations easier to manage. A clinic might offer “Book appointment”, “Change appointment”, and “Speak to reception”. A school might offer “Admissions”, “Fees”, and “Transport”.

Interactive design should reduce effort rather than trap the customer in an automated menu. Provide a clear path to a human when the issue is complex or sensitive.

### Payments, orders, and bookings

An active conversation can include information about an order, appointment, application, or payment. However, WhatsApp messages should not replace proper records in your accounting, CRM, or booking system.

For Indian businesses, be careful with:

- GST invoices and tax details
- Refund commitments
- Payment links
- UPI instructions
- Medical information
- Student records
- Donor and beneficiary data

A WhatsApp reply is not automatically a legally sufficient invoice, consent record, or service agreement. Store important information in the system responsible for that record.

## What Happens After the 24-Hour Window Closes?

Once the window closes, a normal free-form API message may be rejected or blocked. The business generally needs to send an approved template to contact the customer again.

Suppose a customer asks about a D2C product on Monday at 11:00 am. The customer does not reply after your initial answer. On Tuesday afternoon, your team wants to send:

> “Would you like help choosing the correct size?”

Because more than 24 hours have passed since the customer’s last message, this may require an approved template rather than an ordinary session message. Whether the message is suitable also depends on its purpose and the customer’s consent.

### A template does not reopen the window simply because it was delivered

Sending a template is not the same as receiving a customer response. If the customer replies to the template, a new 24-hour customer service window may open from that reply.

For example:

1. The original customer conversation closes.
2. The business sends an approved appointment reminder template.
3. The customer replies, “Can I move this appointment to Friday?”
4. A new customer service window may begin from that customer reply.
5. The team can then respond with free-form session messages during the open period.

Your software should distinguish between a delivered template and a customer response. Treating every outgoing message as a new open session is a common implementation error.

### When a template is not appropriate

Do not use a utility template as a workaround for a marketing message. For example, a sales promotion should not be labelled as an order update merely to avoid marketing requirements.

Similarly, do not send repeated templates to people who have not agreed to receive messages from your organisation. Customers may report unwanted messages, which can affect quality ratings, delivery, and the standing of your WhatsApp Business account.

## Consent, Privacy, and Indian Compliance

The 24-hour window does not remove the need for consent, responsible data handling, or compliance with Indian law.

### Obtain clear opt-in

If you plan to send notifications, reminders, or marketing messages, collect consent in a clear manner. Explain:

- Who will send the messages
- What type of messages the person will receive
- How often messages may be sent, where relevant
- How the person can stop receiving them

A pre-ticked checkbox or unclear statement such as “I agree to updates” may not be suitable for every use case. Keep a record of when and where the person opted in.

Consent collected for order updates does not automatically mean consent for unrelated promotional campaigns. Separate the purposes where necessary.

### Offer an opt-out path

If a customer asks to stop receiving messages, record that request and suppress future non-essential messages. A simple process might recognise words such as “STOP”, but staff should also handle natural language requests such as “Please don’t message me again”.

Do not keep sending messages merely because an old opt-in exists if the customer has clearly withdrawn it.

### Handle personal data carefully

Indian organisations may handle names, phone numbers, addresses, order information, health details, student records, financial information, or donor details through WhatsApp.

Use access controls and avoid exposing personal information in group chats. For clinics, do not send sensitive medical details unless your process is appropriate for the situation. For schools and NGOs, make sure staff know which information can be shared with a parent, guardian, beneficiary, or volunteer.

The Digital Personal Data Protection framework and other applicable Indian laws may affect how you collect, use, retain, and delete personal data. The exact obligations depend on your organisation, data, and processing activities. Obtain legal advice for a high-risk or regulated workflow.

### Do not rely only on WhatsApp

Important customer records should also exist in your internal system. Keep consent logs, ticket history, payment records, appointment details, and opt-out status in a controlled database or CRM.

This makes it easier to manage staff changes, audit communications, answer complaints, and prevent duplicate messages.

## Common Mistakes Businesses Make

### Mistake 1: Starting the timer when the business replies

The timer is not normally based on your outgoing message. A business reply at 3:00 pm does not generally give you another 24 hours.

Your team should record the timestamp of the latest qualifying customer interaction.

### Mistake 2: Treating an open window as permission for promotions

A customer may contact you about a return. That does not necessarily mean you can send a catalogue, festival offer, or unrelated product campaign through the same session.

Keep support and marketing purposes distinct. If you want to run marketing campaigns, use the correct template category, consent process, and audience controls.

### Mistake 3: Waiting until the window closes to ask for basic information

If your workflow needs an order ID, patient appointment number, or application reference, ask for it while the customer is engaged. Waiting for the next day can force your team to use a template before the conversation can continue.

### Mistake 4: Using the wrong template category

A template that contains a discount or product recommendation may be marketing even if it is presented as a reminder. Misclassification can lead to rejection or account-quality problems.

Create a small template library based on real business use cases and review it before submission.

### Mistake 5: Assuming every provider behaves the same way

A WhatsApp Business Solution Provider may add its own dashboard rules, automation settings, or sending restrictions. Some providers queue messages, while others reject them immediately when the window is closed.

Ask how the provider handles:

- Window status
- Failed sends
- Template fallback
- Opt-outs
- Conversation history
- Webhook events
- Media storage
- User access and audit logs

### Mistake 6: Sending too many messages in one session

Even when messages are technically allowed, a rapid series of unnecessary replies can feel intrusive. Combine information where practical, let the customer choose the next step, and avoid sending five separate messages when one clear reply will do.

## Building a Reliable WhatsApp Workflow

A good implementation does not depend on staff remembering the exact time of every customer message.

### Track the last customer interaction

Your CRM or WhatsApp integration should store:

- Customer phone number
- Last incoming message timestamp
- Last outgoing message timestamp
- Current conversation status
- Opt-in source and date
- Opt-out status
- Relevant customer or order ID
- Template messages sent
- Delivery and failure status

The system can then identify whether a session is likely to be open and select the appropriate message type.

### Add a safety check before sending

Before an automated message goes out, check:

1. Has the customer sent a qualifying message within the current window?
2. Is the message relevant to that conversation?
3. Is a template required?
4. If a template is required, is it approved for this purpose?
5. Does the contact have a valid opt-in?
6. Has the person opted out?
7. Does the message include accurate customer or order data?

This is especially important for scheduled jobs such as abandoned-cart reminders, fee reminders, appointment follow-ups, and donation acknowledgements.

### Use human escalation

A bot can answer common questions, but it should hand over issues it cannot resolve. Inform the customer when a human agent is taking over, and preserve the relevant conversation context.

For clinics, schools, and NGOs, escalation may be necessary for sensitive personal matters. For ecommerce brands, it may be necessary for refunds, damaged products, payment disputes, or delivery exceptions.

### Plan for outside-hours enquiries

If your team does not monitor WhatsApp continuously, set an automatic acknowledgement explaining the working hours. A customer may still expect a response, so the message should be honest rather than promising an immediate reply.

For example:

> “We have received your message. Our support team is available Monday to Saturday, 10:00 am to 6:00 pm. We will respond during working hours.”

If the window closes before staff respond, your process should decide whether to send an approved template or wait for the customer to message again.

## Costs and Technical Considerations

The 24-hour rule and WhatsApp charges are related but not identical.

Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform pricing and conversation rules can change. Charges may depend on the message category, country, recipient, business setup, and current commercial model. Service messages within an active customer service window may receive different treatment from business-initiated marketing, utility, or authentication messages.

You may also incur costs from:

- A WhatsApp Business Solution Provider
- CRM or helpdesk software
- Chatbot development
- Message storage
- Agent seats
- Template management
- Integration and maintenance
- GST on applicable services

Do not decide based only on the cost of sending a message. A poorly designed workflow can create operational costs through duplicate messages, manual follow-up, missed enquiries, and failed automation.

For an Indian organisation, ask your provider for a written explanation of:

- Meta-related charges
- Provider fees
- GST treatment
- Template-related charges
- Support and maintenance fees
- Number setup or migration requirements
- What happens if a message fails
- Whether usage limits apply

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does the 24-hour window start when the business sends a message?

Usually, no. It generally starts when the customer sends a message to the business and is measured from the customer’s latest qualifying interaction. A business reply does not normally reset the timer.

### Can I send a promotional message during the open window?

An open window allows free-form replies relevant to the customer’s active conversation. It does not automatically permit unrelated promotions. Marketing messages should follow the correct WhatsApp policy, template, and consent requirements.

### What can I do if the 24-hour window has expired?

Use an approved template that matches the purpose of the message, provided the customer has given the required consent. If the customer replies, a new customer service window may open and the team can generally continue with session messages.

### Does a customer replying to a template reopen the window?

A customer response can open a new 24-hour customer service window. The template being delivered or read does not by itself create the same permission as a customer reply.

### Is the rule the same in the WhatsApp Business app?

The 24-hour API rule is most important for businesses using the WhatsApp Business Platform and automated messaging. The WhatsApp Business app is used differently, but its messages must still follow WhatsApp’s policies and the business should avoid spam or unwanted contact.

### How should I track the window for a team?

Use a CRM, helpdesk, or WhatsApp integration that records the last incoming customer message and displays the current session status. Add checks for opt-in, opt-out, template eligibility, delivery failures, and human escalation.

## Where to Start

Map your main WhatsApp use cases first: support, admissions, appointments, order updates, donations, reminders, or marketing. For each use case, identify whether the customer starts the conversation and what should happen if the 24-hour window closes.

Then select an official WhatsApp Business Platform setup, document your consent process, create only the templates you genuinely need, and connect the conversation to your CRM or internal records. Test scenarios involving weekends, missed replies, opt-outs, failed deliveries, and customer responses to templates.
